explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/751: for G with χ(G) = 4 and cycle lengths m₁ < m₂ < ⋯, can min(m_{i+1} − m_i) be arbitrarily large? No, by Bondy–Vince. The statement negates: for every k there is G (any vertex type) with chromaticNumber = 4 whose distinct cycle lengths all differ by ≥ k. That is exactly 'arbitrarily large minimal gap'. Faithful.
